extracted.intended_audience: Printz Award committee members, YALSA volunteers, librarians serving on award committees, and publishers/submitters
extracted.subtask_description: Official YALSA policies and procedures for selecting the Michael L. Printz Award winner and honor books, including eligibility, evaluation criteria (literary excellence), nomination and voting procedures, committee composition, and ethical/confidentiality rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary definition of the award (literary excellence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Michael L. Printz Award recognizes the best titles in young adult literature in a given calendar year, with 'best' being defined solely in terms of literary merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What is quality? The award hopes for a wide audience but POPULARITY is not the criterion. Nor is MESSAGE. CONTROVERSY is not something to avoid; the committee wants a book that readers will talk about. Flexibility and avoidance of too-rigid criteria are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of popularity and message as criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Popularity and the book's message are explicitly not criteria for the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In accordance with the Library Bill of Rights, controversy is not to be avoided; a book's capacity to provoke discussion can be positive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility; avoid too-rigid criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria change with time; flexibility and avoidance of overly rigid requirements are essential components of the criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of 'too-rigid' criteria to avoid include: insisting on a realistic hope, avoiding complicated plot, or demanding strict originality — many great books violate such constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested evaluation guideline: Story
rubrics_metrics.description: Story is listed as a suggested guideline for evaluating literary excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These listed criteria are only suggested guidelines and not absolutes; the weight of story will vary depending on the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested evaluation guideline: Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice is listed as a suggested guideline for evaluating literary excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice's importance will vary by title; it's one of several sample considerations rather than a strict rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested evaluation guideline: Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Style is listed as a suggested guideline for evaluating literary excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of style should be adapted to each book rather than treated as an absolute requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested evaluation guideline: Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting is listed as a suggested guideline for evaluating literary excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on the work, setting may carry more or less weight in assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested evaluation guideline: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy is listed as a suggested guideline for evaluating literary excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy (factual, contextual, cultural, etc.) should be considered where relevant to the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested evaluation guideline: Characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters is listed as a suggested guideline for evaluating literary excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterization quality is an evaluative axis but not an absolute requirement across all books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested evaluation guideline: Theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Theme is listed as a suggested guideline for evaluating literary excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theme should be assessed within the context of the book's aims and form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested evaluation guideline: Illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations are included among suggested guidelines and may factor into literary merit when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider art and how it contributes to the work's literary qualities (particularly for graphic or illustrated works).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested evaluation guideline: Design (format, organization, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design, including format and organization, is a suggested guideline for evaluating literary excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical/typographic/organizational choices that affect literary experience should be considered as part of merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Publication date window
rubrics_metrics.description: Books must have been published between January 1 and December 31 of the year preceding announcement of the award to be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chair is responsible for verifying eligibility of nominated titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Target audience designation (age 12–18)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible, a title must have been designated by its publisher as being either a young adult book or one published for the age range YALSA defines as 'young adult,' i.e., 12 through 18. Adult books are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher designation is the determinative factor for age-target eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Allowed formats and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The award-winning book may be fiction, nonfiction, poetry or an anthology. Works of joint authorship or editorship are eligible. The award may be given posthumously provided other criteria are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All forms of writing—fiction, nonfiction, poetry, art, and any combination including anthologies—are eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Previously published abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: Books previously published in another country are eligible, presuming an American edition has been published during the period of eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An American edition within the eligibility window qualifies the title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility restriction: self-published, ebook-only, or non-US publisher distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles that are self-published, published only in eBook format, and/or published from a publisher outside of the US will not be considered eligible until the first year the book is available in print or distributed through a US publishing house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restricts eligibility until a US print/distribution presence exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: No award if no sufficiently meritorious title
rubrics_metrics.description: If no title is deemed sufficiently meritorious, no award will be given that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee may decide to give zero awards rather than lower standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominations by committee members
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members may nominate an unlimited number of titles, but each nomination must be made in writing on an official nomination form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each nomination should include author, title, publisher, price, ISBN, and an annotation specifying those qualities that justify the title for consideration. Nominations from committee members need no second.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field suggestions procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Field suggestions are encouraged but must be submitted on the official suggestion form and must be seconded by a committee member; if no second is forthcoming within thirty days the title will be dropped from consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only those titles that have been nominated (and seconded if field suggestions) may be discussed at Midwinter and Annual Conference meetings. Furthermore, all nominated titles must be discussed. Publishers, authors, or editors may not suggest or nominate their own titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of nominations and deliberations
rubrics_metrics.description: All nominated titles must be kept confidential; there will be no announcements of nominated titles. All committee meetings and discussions, including electronic discussions, are closed to YALSA membership and the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This covers both in-person and electronic communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee composition and appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee shall consist of a chair, eight members, a consultant from the staff of Booklist, and an administrative assistant if the Chair requests. Beginning in 2017, the Chair and members will be appointed by the Vice President/President-Elect of YALSA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee size: 9 members, plus a Booklist consultant and optional administrative assistant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee term length and attendance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Members serve 12-month terms beginning February 1 and ending January 31 of the following year. All members are required to attend all Printz Committee meetings held during the selection process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a member cannot complete the term, the President (in consultation) shall appoint a qualified replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair role and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The chair is a voting member with all rights and responsibilities of other members, presides at meetings, facilitates discussion and committee business, must serve as list owner of an electronic discussion list, and take responsibility for list maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chair also assembles and distributes lists of nominated titles at specified calendar milestones and coordinates with the administrative assistant if appointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative assistant and Booklist consultant roles
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrative assistant, if appointed, will assist the chair (contacting publishers, maintaining nomination database, tabulating votes) and is a non-voting YALSA member; the Booklist consultant may participate fully in book discussions but may not participate in voting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative assistant must be a YALSA member; consultant is appointed by Booklist magazine (sponsor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service/appointment limits for committee members
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members, including administrative assistants and chairs, who have completed one full term on any of YALSA’s six award committees may not be appointed to the same or another YALSA award committee for two years from the conclusion of their term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may be made in extreme circumstances at the President’s discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee member responsibilities and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Members are required to attend all committee meetings and read widely from books eligible for nomination. All committee members must comply with YALSA's Policies, including Social Media Policy, Ethical Behavior Policy for Volunteers and the Award Committees Conflict of Interest Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional information about responsibilities is available in YALSA's Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical behavior and publisher interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: The chair and/or administrative assistant are responsible for contact with publishers. Committee members must not solicit publishers for free personal copies of books. If members receive, or are offered, unsolicited copies of books from publishers, they may accept the titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must not solicit publishers for favors, invitations, etc. If such offers are received, members should use their judgment in accepting; acceptance does not influence selections. See YALSA Ethical Behavior Policy and Conflict of Interest Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calendar and deadlines for committee workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: General calendar items: May–June appointments; December virtual training; February 1 committee begins work; by May 15 chair sends list of nominated titles; June ALA Annual Conference three closed sessions; September 15 chair sends list of titles nominated since Annual; December 1 final date for submission of field nominations; December 15 final date for nominations by committee members; January 1 chair sends list of titles nominated since September 15; January Midwinter Meeting selection sessions; February input into planning; June Annual Conference Printz Awards Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair develops and shares detailed timeline; committee observes these milestones as general rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting procedures: straw votes and balloting mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Straw votes may be conducted at the chair's discretion to guide discussion. Members must be present to vote; proxies will not be accepted. Following discussion, paper ballots are used. On each ballot each member votes for top three choices: first choice receives 5 points, second 3 points, third 1 point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members are reminded that at this point they are voting for the winner, not for honor titles. Paper ballots will be tallied by the chair or designees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winning threshold for the award
rubrics_metrics.description: To win, a title must receive five first-place votes and must also receive at least five more points than the second-place title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no title meets these criteria on the first ballot, any title receiving no votes is removed and discussion and further balloting continue until a winner is declared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor books selection process
rubrics_metrics.description: All nominated titles are eligible for honor book consideration. Following selection of a winner, a straw vote is conducted and any title receiving no votes is removed from consideration. A formal, weighted ballot will follow. Based on results, the committee will decide if it wishes to name honor books and how many.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honor book balloting is separate from the winner ballot and follows similar elimination/weighting procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotations and press release requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee is responsible for writing a press release and annotations for the winning title and honor books. Both the annotations and the press release will include discussion of the literary merits of the titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The annotations and press release must be written prior to the Monday awards press conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seals licensing and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers wishing to buy bulk seals or license seal images should consult YALSA's Award Seals Usage Guidelines and ALA's Seals Sales & Permissions page. Individuals can buy small quantities of seals via the ALA Online Store.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance and links provided for licensing and purchasing award seals for winners/honors.
